approachQuestion.prompt:
Three Operators

Between each adjacent pair of digits in a nonempty decimal digit string, insert exactly one operator from +, -, *. Do not concatenate digits and do not add parentheses. Return every resulting expression whose integer value equals target, using usual multiplication precedence. Each expression appears once.

Examples:
digits="123", target=7 -> ["1+2*3"].
digits="12", target=2 -> ["1*2"].
digits="0", target=0 -> ["0"].

Constraints: 1 <= n=digits.length <= 10; each character is a digit 0..9; -1000000000 <= target <= 1000000000. All intermediate values fit signed 64-bit integers.

options.text: Carry the evaluated total and the last signed term. On multiplication, replace that last term by its product with the next digit; try all three operators at each gap.
options.feedback: The last signed term is exactly the part that multiplication must extend before addition or subtraction. This keeps precedence correct without reevaluating the full prefix.

options.text: Evaluate every new operator immediately from left to right using only the running total.
options.feedback: For digits="123", "1+2*3" is 7, but left-to-right evaluation produces 9 and can miss the required expression.

options.text: Treat subtraction as a negative total but store the last digit as a positive lastTerm.
options.feedback: For digits="123", "1-2*3" must be -5. A positive lastTerm=2 after the subtraction makes the replacement formula produce 3 instead.

options.text: Enumerate all operator strings and evaluate each full expression with a fresh precedence-aware parser.
options.feedback: This is correct for all inputs, but repeatedly rescans long expressions; constant-size running arithmetic state removes that work.

feedback.reason: The last signed term is exactly the part that multiplication must extend before addition or subtraction. This keeps precedence correct without reevaluating the full prefix.
details: Initialize total and lastTerm from the first digit. At every gap branch over the three operators. For a next digit d, addition sets (total+d,d), subtraction (total-d,-d), and multiplication (total-lastTerm+lastTerm*d,lastTerm*d). Copy matching expressions only after the last gap.

lastTerm retains the signed multiplication chain. Replace that term inside total when multiplying, so multiplication binds tighter than prior addition/subtraction. Undo buffer changes without recomputing the entire expression prefix.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-09-search` only. Let R be the number of characters copied into returned expressions. Use a mutable expression buffer and constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. The method visits all three branches at each of n-1 gaps, even if no expression matches. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(3ⁿ + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n·3ⁿ + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(3ⁿ + R) time, O(3ⁿ) auxiliary space
O(n + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Three choices per gap create exponential search work plus copied matching expressions.
details: The full ternary tree has a geometric sum of calls proportional to 3^(n-1), equivalent to 3ⁿ up to constants. Each edge updates constant-size arithmetic state; copying matching buffers adds R.
The expression buffer has 2n-1 characters and recursion depth n. Arithmetic state per frame is constant.

Let R be the number of characters copied into returned expressions. Use a mutable expression buffer and constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. The method visits all three branches at each of n-1 gaps, even if no expression matches.
“O(n·3ⁿ + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The revealed method never parses each complete expression from scratch.
“O(3ⁿ + R) time, O(3ⁿ) auxiliary space”: It does not store the full search tree.
“O(n + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: All operator combinations are examined, including unsuccessful ones.
